reason: This gap addresses an important methodological issue in comparing data sources used for studying SUID (Sudden Unexpected Infant Death). The study aims to understand how pregnancy weight gain and postpartum smoking status are recorded differently between the NCFRP case series and PRAMS population reference, which can affect the validity of comparisons made using these datasets. This is crucial because discrepancies in recording methods could introduce bias into analyses comparing SUID cases with a general population sample.
